fix: raw webhook send error

Fix an error where sending structured data through the webhook fails due to unserializable objects.

This fix simply replaces dictionary values that are not JSON-serializable from `data`. A more explicit way might be to sanitize input to `_send_webhook_raw(...)` beforehand.

The error occurs in simpletuner/helpers/training/trainer.py, as the `Trainer.state` dictionary includes unserializable objects, such as a `ProjectConfiguration` instance.
```python
[...]

if (
                        self.config.webhook_reporting_interval is not None
                        and self.state["global_step"]
                        % self.config.webhook_reporting_interval
                        == 0
                    ):
                        structured_data = {
                            "state": self.state,
                            "loss": round(self.train_loss, 4),
                            "parent_loss": parent_loss,
                            "learning_rate": self.lr,
                            "epoch": epoch,
                            "final_epoch": self.config.num_train_epochs,
                        }
                        self._send_webhook_raw(
                            structured_data=structured_data, message_type="train"
                        )

[...]
```

Error log:
```
[ERROR] Could not send webhook request: Object of type ProjectConfiguration is not JSON serializable
```

qwen image: pad text embeds and masks to max seq length before collate

When training with batch_size > 1, QwenImage text sequences can have
different lengths (e.g. 312 vs 287 tokens). The existing collate_prompt_embeds()
calls torch.cat on unpadded tensors, raising RuntimeError for shape mismatch.

Fix: before torch.cat, pad all embeds to max_seq_len (zero-pad hidden dim)
and all masks to max_seq_len (False-pad = masked out). Only activates for
multi-sample batches; single-sample fast path is unchanged.

Fixes batch_size>1 training crash for QwenImage models.

qwen image: per-sample split attention for variable-length batched training

When batch_size > 1, QwenImage text sequences have different lengths.
After padding (collate fix), the joint-mask approach still fails because
it broadcasts one mask for all samples — padding tokens from shorter
sequences contaminate attention scores of longer ones, producing
corrupted outputs (desaturated mannequins by step ~50).

This commit introduces three coordinated changes:

1. model.py (collate): pad embeds + masks to max_seq_len before torch.cat
2. transformer.py (forward + processor): when batch_size > 1 and a mask
   is present, run per-sample attention — slice each sample's text Q/K/V
   to its true length, run unmasked attention per-sample, then re-stack.
   For batch_size == 1, the existing efficient joint-mask path is unchanged.
3. pipeline.py: preserve all-ones masks instead of discarding them. The
   mask is the routing signal for split attention; discarding it forces
   fallback to joint attention even when batch > 1.

Approach follows musubi-tuner PR #688 (merged) which solved the same
variable-length text sequence problem for a different model.

Tested: batch_size=4, diffusers attention, Prodigy optimizer, 300+ steps
clean with no corruption (baseline corrupted at step ~50 without fix).

wan: fix time_text_monkeypatch missing timestep_sign argument

  The transformer forward at wan/transformer.py:846 unconditionally passes
  timestep_sign= to self.condition_embedder for every Wan forward pass.
  Commit 07e670c4 ('TwinFlow: Wan') added that argument to the call site
  but did not update the time_text_monkeypatch signature in wan/model.py,
  causing every Wan training/validation forward to raise:

    TypeError: time_text_monkeypatch() got an unexpected keyword argument
    'timestep_sign'

  This patch brings the monkeypatch in sync with the vendored
  WanTimeTextImageEmbedding.forward (wan/transformer.py:253-290): it
  accepts timestep_sign, derives timestep_seq_len from timestep.shape
  when needed, and applies the time-sign embedding when the embedder
  has time_sign_embed enabled (TwinFlow path). The previously dead
  timestep_seq_len kwarg is removed since the call site never passes it.

  Adds a regression test asserting the monkeypatch accepts timestep_sign.

Fix safetensors checkpoint corruption caused by memory-mapped in-place overwrite

When _append_metadata_to_safetensors() reads tensors via safe_open()
and then re-saves them to the same file path, the tensors are memory-mapped
views into the original file. Writing to the same path truncates the file
while the tensors still point at the now-invalid file memory, resulting in
corrupted checkpoint data (all values become zero or extreme magnitudes
like 1e-19 to 1e37 instead of normal bf16 magnitudes).

This causes all periodic checkpoint LoRA weights (subdirectory checkpoints
like checkpoint-XXX/pytorch_lora_weights.safetensors) to produce completely
black images during inference, while the root-level save (which skips this
method) remains unaffected.

Fix: clone each tensor after reading to break the memory-mapped reference
before overwriting the file.

Fix single-file SD/SDXL export with flattened CLIPTextModel (transformers >=5.6)

transformers 5.6 (huggingface/transformers#44431) flattened CLIPTextModel,
removing the `text_model.` submodule wrapper. The convert_sd*/convert_sdxl
export tables and the SD v2.0 detection probe still expect the nested keys,
so single-file export from a 5.6+ diffusers checkpoint produced broken
SD/SDXL files. Restore the `text_model.` prefix on flat text-encoder state
dicts right after load; nested checkpoints (and CLIPTextModelWithProjection,
which was not flattened) pass through unchanged.

restore_clip_text_model_prefix currently prefixes every key when no key starts with text_model.. That can unintentionally rewrite non-CLIPTextModel parameters (e.g. top-level keys like text_projection.* in CLIPTextModelWithProjection, or any future/alt state-dict layouts) and produce an invalid export. It’s safer to only add text_model. for the known flattened CLIPTextModel submodules (embeddings.*, encoder.*, final_layer_norm.*) and otherwise leave the dict untouched.

pre-sigmoid normal sample in the default logit-normal flow-matching schedule,

granularity.

(structure). Default 0.0 = stock behavior.

metal-flash-attention: update api for new constants and masked attention API

feat: route UMFA through the SDPA dispatcher; extend parity checks; lift causal-training gate

- Metal Flash Attention calls now go through PyTorch's SDPA dispatcher
  (which current UMFA builds register on the MPS key) instead of calling
  extension autograd entrypoints directly, so fp32/int8/int4 profiles all
  use UMFA's registered mask-aware path.
- Startup parity checks now cover fp16/bf16 forward and autograd plus
  causal forward against a CPU reference, and get_dispatch_stats() is
  required unconditionally since dispatcher routing depends on it.
- Eligibility no longer rejects supported MPS masks, fp16/bf16 inputs,
  small verified shapes, or causal calls that require gradients — UMFA's
  causal backward passes exact dQ/dK/dV parity on both transposed masking
  codegen paths, so causal training dispatches through UMFA.
- Remaining fallbacks: dropout and enable_gqa.

docs: update Metal Flash Attention docs to current capabilities

Rewrites the stale eligibility description (previously 'unmasked, at
least four heads, sequence length 64+') across OPTIONS and the
experimental UMFA guide, in all six languages:

- Dispatcher-based routing with in-stream encoding: any head count
  (single-head works), any sequence length, bool/additive masks up to 4D,
  causal calls with and without gradients (causal backward passes exact
  gradient parity). Fallbacks are dropout and enable_gqa.
- fp16/bf16 run native low-precision kernels with no fp32 promotion;
  mixed_precision bf16 no longer needs fp32 overrides, and the enable
  example drops the old fp32 pinning.
- Mask support documented for the regular dispatcher (not just
  quantized), including the all-true fast path and in-stream expansion.
- Dispatch counters: fp32_instream for unquantized runs, rope_instream
  for the fused entry point, quantized_autograd for the aliases.
- New fused RoPE + SDPA section: rope_scaled_dot_product_attention
  covering the shared interleaved-pair convention of FLUX.1/FLUX.2/
  Krea2/Z-Image, pair-duplicated [S,D]/[1,S,D]/[B,S,D] tables, strided
  views, fused autograd with inverse rotation on dQ/dK, and the measured
  4.4 ms/layer gain at the Z-Image DiT shape.

fix(training): coordinate FSDP2 gradient measurement and clipping

FSDP2 gradients are DTensors, so rank-local maxima can under-report the
logical gradient, empty local shards must still join collectives, and
reporting must not receive device tensors. The training loop also measured
a max on every accumulation microstep even when norm clipping would
immediately recompute and overwrite it.

- In Trainer._max_grad_value(), measure non-empty local shards, contribute
  negative infinity for empty DTensor shards, stage CPU scalars on the mesh
  device, and all-reduce MAX once across the mesh.
- At synchronized optimizer steps, reuse the norm returned by clipping in
  norm mode and run the separate max path only when clipping does not
  already provide the reported value.
- Preserve existing FSDP1, FSDP2, non-FSDP, optimizer-exclusion, and FSDP
  value-clipping policies while avoiding duplicate gradient traversal and
  collectives.
- Normalize norm and max values through one scalar path for logs, progress,
  webhooks, and regularisation metrics.

fix(training): correct FSDP2 CPU-offload tensor placement

Current Accelerate calls the FSDP2 full-state loader with a cpu_offload
argument, while older callers use the previous three-argument form. The local
override handled neither combination safely under an active offload policy.

- Extend the replacement loader signature with an optional cpu_offload value so
  both current and legacy call forms remain valid.
- When the argument is omitted, infer placement from the active
  CPUOffloadPolicy; explicit true and false continue to override that policy.
- Apply the resolved placement to sharded and unsharded tensors on main and
  non-main ranks before load_state_dict(assign=True). This keeps parameter
  placement consistent across the complete FSDP2 model.
- Keep CPU placement independent of RAM-efficient loading because offload is an
  FSDP2 runtime policy rather than a loader memory-mode side effect.

fix(training): preserve gradient metric logging contracts

Restore the clone_norm_value keyword used by existing callers and keep value-mode grad_absmax entries as the original metric object. Continue converting norm metrics to scalars only for progress payloads that explicitly request cloning.

This keeps the FSDP2 mesh-wide max reduction and synchronized clipping changes while preserving the pre-existing logging API and tensor identity behavior exercised by the upstream trainer suite.

fix(training): export portable FSDP2 pipelines safely

Unwrapping an FSDP2 component on rank zero does not reconstruct its full
DTensor state, so direct Diffusers pipeline export can be incomplete. Final
save failures also need a shared result across every participating rank.

- In training/save_hooks.py, preflight the trained component, registered
  pipeline slot, exact config reconstruction, and Accelerate version before
  FSDP2 preparation. Unsupported exports now fail before a full training run.
- Collectively materialize a CPU non-DTensor state, validate EMA parameter
  correspondence, and retain the full state only on the main rank. Every rank
  joins reconstruction without retaining a redundant host copy.
- Rebuild a save-only component on meta, strict-load the gathered state, and
  temporarily replace the registered pipeline component for save_pretrained().
  Restore the live sharded component in finally on success or failure.
- In training/trainer.py, run preflight before distributed wrapping, make every
  rank join get_state_dict(..., unwrap=False), and keep pipeline serialization
  on the main rank only.
- Guard final export with a scalar all-reduce so peer ranks observe a remote
  failure while the rank that raised preserves its original exception.

test(data): cover conditioning duplication and empty-bucket splits

Regression coverage for two behaviours this branch already implements but
does not test.

copy_metadata no longer reloads the source cache and marks the target
read-only before persisting anything (duplicator.py). The new
conditioning test drives all eight ranks through a real split with
padding, with the unsplit source cache present on disk, and asserts that
every rank keeps its shard, that the shards still cover the dataset, that
the conditioning dataset inherits the same shard, and that the shared
conditioning cache never becomes rank-dependent.

split_buckets_between_processes skips empty buckets before the repeat
arithmetic (base.py). The new metadata test pins that across world sizes
1/2/8 and both oversubscription settings, keeps the pre-existing "zero
usable batches" error for the flag-off case, and pins the
update_buckets_with_existing_files behaviour that leaves the empty key
behind in the first place.

The oversubscription assertions follow this branch's semantics: repeats
is left unmutated and the auto repeat factor is materialised into the
rank-local cyclic shard instead.

fix(data): only restore a checkpointed shard when every rank has one

load_states restored the checkpointed aspect_ratio_bucket_indices
unconditionally, but that dict is one rank's shard. Under plain DDP only
rank 0 reaches checkpoint_state_save, so on resume rank 0 replayed its
old shard while the other ranks re-split against a fresh per-launch
shuffle seed: the ranks stopped partitioning the dataset. Nothing
recorded the data-parallel layout either, so resuming onto a different
world size restored shards that no longer matched the run.

save_state now records the effective DP size and rank, and the schedule
is restored only when that layout still matches and the checkpoint holds
a state file for every rank. Checkpoints without the layout are left
alone, which is what load_states did before the schedule restore existed.

fix(data): keep post-split shard length when filtering a sample

_handle_metadata_filtered_sample removes every occurrence of the filtered
path from the live bucket list. After a padded split that list is this
rank's shard, whose length is a distributed invariant, and the padding
tail repeats one item -- so a single filter event can shorten or empty
the shard while its DP peers keep theirs.

The removal itself is unchanged: a problematic or NSFW sample must not be
trained on. The slots it vacated are refilled by repeating the final
surviving sample, which is the rule the splitter already uses to pad. A
bucket the filter emptied has nothing left to repeat and stays empty
until the next split re-derives it from the shortened cache.

fix(training): write LoRA checkpoints in PEFT naming

_save_lora passed the denoiser adapter through diffusers'
convert_state_dict_to_diffusers(), whose PEFT_TO_DIFFUSERS table only
renames to_q/to_k/to_v/to_out.0. Any target outside attention kept its
PEFT name, so a wide-target checkpoint was written with two naming
schemes in one file. diffusers decides whether to convert back from a
single key, guesses wrong on such a file, and silently drops every
diffusers-named tensor.

Write get_peft_model_state_dict() verbatim instead, matching the
controlnet branch five lines above and the final export in trainer.py.

convert_diffusers_to_comfyui() emitted .alpha only inside its
.lora.down. branch, so it must normalise both spellings before deriving
alpha or ComfyUI exports would lose every alpha once checkpoints are
PEFT-named.

Fix fp32 dtype leak from QK-norm in Flux2 attention processors

torch.nn.RMSNorm is on autocast's fp32 promotion list, so under
autocast(bf16) or autocast(fp16) the QK-norm layers in Flux2Attention
return fp32 tensors while the value tensor remains in half precision.

apply_rotary_emb preserves the wider dtype, so query/key reach the
attention backend as fp32 alongside a half-precision value. Backends
that require a uniform half dtype reject this outright -- flash-attn
raises on mismatched input dtypes rather than casting.

Cast the normalised query/key back to the dtype of the corresponding
value tensor. Using value.dtype rather than a hardcoded bfloat16 keeps
the fix correct under fp16 autocast and in full-precision runs, where
the cast becomes a no-op.

Applies to both Flux2AttnProcessor (including the added_kv_proj_dim
encoder path) and Flux2ParallelSelfAttnProcessor.

Track the skipped-caption count separately and cover both Webshart-caption and filename-caption behavior in metadata backend tests.

Report capped video dataset totals in sampler overviews

Honor max_num_samples when the sampler builds model-card overview statistics for multi-process jobs so the displayed sample total does not exceed the configured cap.

Read nested video frame and FPS settings when legacy flat fields are absent, and show unknown values explicitly instead of rendering None.

Handle TensorBoard video logging without moviepy

Detect TensorBoard video writer support before passing 5D validation tensors to add_video, because installs without the legacy moviepy.editor module reject video media.

When video logging is unavailable, log the first frame as an image so validation summaries still render instead of failing the tracker path.

Translate Webshart dataloader updates

Update the localized dataloader guides to match the Webshart shard-cache and bucket oversubscription behavior documented in the English guide.

Document that shard_cache_gb=0 disables whole-shard caching while preserving indexed range reads, and clarify that automatic oversubscription pads only undersized aspect buckets instead of increasing repeats globally.

Handle SDNQ fake-mode detection failures

Keep the SDNQ double-quantization workaround active when importing or calling torch fake-mode detection fails for reasons other than a missing import.

Returning None from the detection helper preserves the existing dequantize-before-requantize behavior instead of letting an auxiliary fake-mode check break quantization setup.

Expose DDP unused-parameter detection in the UI registry

Register find_unused_parameters as an advanced CUDA hardware field so users can opt into DistributedDataParallel unused-parameter detection from generated configs.

Add command-line parsing coverage for explicit true, explicit false, and unset values.

Support RamTorch streaming for scaled FP8 linear layers

Add a CPU bouncing FP8 linear module that keeps frozen float8 weights and per-row scales on CPU while transferring and dequantizing only for the forward/backward matmul.

Teach RamTorch replacement to detect scaled FP8 linears, add tests for output and gradient parity, and allow distributed runs to disable shared CPU parameter attachment when that path is unsuitable.

Prepare Musubi block swap models for DDP

Move trainable parameters to the accelerator before DDP wrapping while marking frozen streamed parameters and buffers to be ignored by DDP.

Enable gradient_as_bucket_view when block swapping is active, preserve existing unused-parameter behavior through a shared DDP kwargs path, and add tests for frozen-state ignore handling.

Synchronize standalone context-parallel training batches

Broadcast sampled batches only within the model-replica group and run batch preparation under a replica-local RNG seed so context-parallel shards share stochastic conditioning.

Scale standalone context-parallel losses before DDP averaging, including activation-offload probes, and add runtime tests for replica grouping, synchronized RNG, and FSDP exclusion.

Handle standalone prefetch autotune without CP topology

Let activation-offload prefetch autotune treat a missing context-parallel topology as standalone training before scaling the probe loss.

This keeps the real model_predict/backward autotune probe usable in lightweight trainer initialization paths while preserving the context-parallel loss scaling path when topology metadata is present.

Allow CP batch RNG sync without an explicit seed

Pass a missing trainer seed through to the context-parallel batch RNG synchronizer instead of assuming every lightweight config namespace defines one.

This preserves deterministic CP sampling when a seed is configured while keeping trainer test scaffolds and startup paths compatible with standalone defaults.

Allow process group timeout overrides from the environment

Distributed startup previously used a fixed 90-minute process-group timeout for every run. Longer multi-node startup paths can need a larger timeout, while invalid shorter values should fail early instead of reaching accelerator setup with confusing behavior.

Read SIMPLETUNER_PROCESS_GROUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS during argument parsing, validate that it is positive, and pass the resulting timedelta through InitProcessGroupKwargs. Cover the default, override, and invalid override cases in the command-argument unittest suite.

Add rank-local training diagnostics hooks

Distributed training failures can leave little rank-local context when compile caches collide or a worker hangs. Add opt-in launch helpers for per-rank TorchInductor cache directories and faulthandler logs without changing the default training path.

SIMPLETUNER_RANK_LOCAL_INDUCTOR_CACHE_ROOT now assigns TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR under a rank-specific child directory before trainer imports. SIMPLETUNER_FAULTHANDLER_DIR enables rank-local traceback output, and SIMPLETUNER_FAULTHANDLER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS can request repeated traceback dumps for stalled workers.

Cover the cache and faulthandler helper behavior in the train-entry unittest suite.

Run startup validation after checkpoint resume

Validation on startup previously ran before restored training state was available in the standalone train entrypoint. That meant resumed jobs could validate with stale step context or skip the same path that Trainer.misc_init uses.

Move startup validation behind resume_and_prepare in the train entrypoint and expose a shared Trainer helper that uses the restored global step. Add focused coverage for enabled and disabled startup validation, plus the entrypoint call order before train() starts.

Run base benchmark validation in eval mode

Base-model benchmark generation was running through validation while the trained component could still be in training mode. That leaves dropout or training-only module behavior active during benchmark renders and can also leave the model in the wrong mode if validation raises.

Switch the trained component to eval mode around the base benchmark validation, run validation under accelerator autocast, save the benchmark, and restore training mode in a finally block when the component started in training mode. Cover the normal and error paths in focused trainer tests.

Restore constant-with-warmup LR on resume

Checkpoint resume already repaired optimizer and scheduler LR state for the constant scheduler, but constant_with_warmup uses the same fixed post-warmup learning rate once training resumes. Leaving it out could restore stale scheduler state from the checkpoint after a learning-rate override.

Treat constant_with_warmup like constant when reapplying the configured learning rate during resume, and add a regression test that verifies optimizer param groups plus scheduler base_lrs and _last_lr are restored.

Initialize distillation adapter modules before PEFT setup

Distillation modules that contribute adapter targets need to be registered before PEFT adapter initialization scans trainable modules. In the standalone train entrypoint, that registration previously happened only after the PEFT adapter setup path had already run.

Call init_distillation_adapter_modules before init_trainable_peft_adapter in the train entrypoint, and extend the entrypoint unittest to assert the ordering remains adapter-module setup, PEFT setup, then distillation setup.

Refactor ComfyUI LoRA conversion through model hooks

ComfyUI LoRA conversion had model-family conditionals embedded in the common save path, which made format support brittle as model-specific naming rules diverged. Move the conversion decisions behind model hooks while preserving the existing SD, SDXL, Flux-family, and transformer-prefix behavior.

The common loader now routes ComfyUI input conversion through a model hook, save_lora_weights delegates ComfyUI output conversion through the same model foundation boundary, and denoiser loading raises when every denoiser tensor is rejected as unexpected. Existing LoRA metadata tests cover the ComfyUI prefix and SDXL/Kohya conversion behavior.

Preserve validation context in text embed cache

Validation prompt encoding needs to preserve whether the current encode is for validation, because some model implementations vary text conditioning behavior between training and validation paths. The cache path also needs to preserve model-specific collator behavior when returning multiple cached records with auxiliary tensors.

Thread the validation flag through uncached text embedding generation, temporarily mark the model while validation prompts are encoded, and use the model collator for multi-record cached outputs. The text embedding tests cover validation context, rank-local record handling, and extra tensor collation.

Respect active model dropout cache policy in collate

Caption dropout can route empty prompts through the default text embedding cache. For path-keyed caches, the decision to use the dropout sentinel belongs to the active model being trained, not necessarily the model attached to the default cache object.

Pass the active model into single-prompt embedding computation in both serial and threaded paths, and use that model when deciding whether to replace an empty prompt key with the dropout sentinel. The collate tests cover preserving the dataset key when the active model disables sentinel usage.

Enable AnyFlow CFG conditioning support

AnyFlow can require unconditional text embeddings when fused CFG guidance is enabled, but the training path did not consistently advertise or cache those requirements before collation and validation. That left CFG distillation paths without the negative or unconditional conditioning needed to build guided targets.

Add distiller batch-requirement hooks, pre-PEFT FlowMap preparation, unconditional embedding collation, image-context dropout prompt cache entries, validation scheduler delegation, and sidecar loading for FlowMap adapter tensors. Update the AnyFlow docs and example config to reflect CFG-capable training.

Improve AnyFlow target geometry and CFG conditioning

MeanFlow targets need stable per-branch geometry diagnostics and consistent conditioning when classifier-free guidance is fused into the objective. The earlier path could replace the raw flow target too early and did not cover the prompt-conditioning and collate interactions used by guided AnyFlow runs.

Keep raw and guided targets separate, add chunked per-sample geometry metrics, cap non-diffusion sigma ranges, support unconditional embeddings in collate and FlowMap sidecars, and cover the target geometry, CFG, and FlowMap conditioning paths in tests. The main-based test uses generic AnyFlow config shapes instead of an H3-only nested distiller.

Preserve generic flow custom timestep conversion

Custom flow validation timesteps should use a model-specific sigma-to-timestep converter when one exists, but generic flow-matching models still need a fallback that preserves normalized timesteps or rescales scheduler-step values correctly. Requiring every model to provide the converter breaks generic flow tests and non-specialized validation paths.

Add a local conversion helper in the trainer override path, use the model converter when present, and otherwise apply the standard flow-matching convention. Apply the same conversion to audio timesteps so mixed modality batches keep their timestep representation aligned.

anyflow: swap unconditional aliases instead of popping them

Flux keys its text conditioning on prompt_embeds, so popping the alias in
_unconditional_batch crashed any run using real_score_guidance_scale > 0
with KeyError at model_predict. Replacing the alias with the negative
embeds (and alias masks with the negative mask when cached) serves both
families: Ideogram's proxy path reads the same negative tensor it used to
fall back to, and Flux keeps the key it requires.

Note: the unconditional pass still reuses the positive pooled projection
for Flux since collation does not cache a negative pooled embed.

anyflow: cache and swap negative pooled embeds for the unconditional pass

Collation now carries the unconditional pooled projection as
negative_add_text_embeds, prepare_batch moves it to the accelerator, and
_unconditional_batch swaps it into add_text_embeds and
added_cond_kwargs.text_embeds so Flux and SDXL-style conditioning no
longer reuse the positive pooled embed during unconditional scoring.

Fix regional compilation not executing under mixed precision

`prepare_model` installs its mixed-precision `forward` as an instance attribute bound to the module it was handed;
`compile_regions` copies that binding onto its twin. The twin re-enters the uncompiled original, so regional
compilation never runs and gradient checkpointing set after `prepare()` is inert. Re-bind `forward` and
`_original_forward` onto the module `prepare` returned. The defect is accelerate's; this helper is a no-op once
accelerate re-binds the twin itself.

Cover DDP wrappers in rebind_prepared_forward

Under DDP prepare() returns the DistributedDataParallel wrapper, which has no instance forward; the stale binding sits on
the inner twin one level down, so the top-level rebind was a no-op there. Walk `.module` wrappers and rebind at each level
that still points at the original. Two gloo DDP tests cover the rebind and the no-op once accelerate rebinds the twin itself.

Extend metadata-only bucketing to still images in the discovery backend

Metadata-only bucketing already exists, but not for still images scanned
from a local directory. Videos skip decoding via ffprobe, and the parquet,
huggingface and webshart backends read dimensions from metadata columns.
With the discovery backend on a plain image folder, every file is fully
read and decoded just to reach image.size.

Bucketing never needs those pixels: calculate_target_size() and the crop
coordinate maths derive everything from original_size, and PreparedSample
stores no pixel-derived metadata. On a network filesystem this means a
multi-megabyte read per image for data that is discarded immediately, and
the only way to avoid it today is to maintain an external parquet of
dimensions the file headers already contain.

Still images now take the same metadata-only path as videos.
use_metadata_only is already supported downstream -- TrainingSample
tolerates image=None, since crop() and the transform helper both guard on
`self.image is not None`, and meets_resolution_requirements() has an
image_metadata branch reading original_size. So this adds the entry point
plus a header probe.

_probe_image_dimensions() opens the file with PIL, which parses only the
header; pixel data is loaded lazily and never requested.

The two per-media guards are folded into one
_should_use_metadata_only(is_video_file), so the face-crop exclusion lives
in one place instead of being duplicated. is_video_file is passed
explicitly so a video-extension file inside an IMAGE dataset still falls
back to a full decode. Verified equivalent to the previous logic across
all 480 combinations of file kind, dataset type, ffprobe availability,
backend type, crop flag and crop style.

Guards follow the existing video precedent: local backends only, IMAGE and
CONDITIONING dataset types, never with crop_style="face" (the one crop
style whose coordinates depend on pixel content), and any header read
failure falls back to a full decode.

EXIF orientations 5-8 transpose the image, so header dimensions are
swapped relative to exif_transpose() on the decode path. The orientation
tag is in the header, so it is applied here. Verified equal to the
full-decode result for all eight orientations plus JPEG/PNG/WebP without
EXIF, with corrupt headers falling back as intended.

fix(quantisation): QuantoLoraConv2d.__init__ omits the required use_dora argument

QuantoLoraConv2d defines its own update_layer with use_dora as a required
positional parameter, but __init__ calls it with only six arguments:

    self.update_layer(adapter_name, r, lora_alpha, lora_dropout, init_lora_weights, use_rslora)

so constructing the layer raises

    TypeError: update_layer() missing 1 required positional argument: 'use_dora'

QuantoLoraConv2d is the QConv2d entry in custom_module_mapping and is
instantiated by dispatch_default, so quanto LoRA on any model with Conv2d
layers cannot be set up at all.

use_dora is already a parameter of __init__ (guarded to False just above), and
update_layer uses it to drive dora_init and the self.use_dora bookkeeping, so
passing it through is what the method was written to receive.
